A trader buys goods at a 20% discount on the marked price. He marks them up such that after giving a 10% cash discount on his new marked price, he achieves a net profit of 35% on his actual purchase cost. What is the percentage by which his new marked price is above the original marked price?

A milkman purchases 50 litres of milk at Rs. 36 per litre. He adds 10 litres of water freely available. He sells 40 litres of the mixture at Rs. 40 per litre and the remaining at Rs. 35 per litre, while offering a 5% cash discount on all final bills. What is his total profit?

A merchant uses a faulty balance that weighs 950g for every 1 kg. He marks his goods 40% above the cost price, offers a 10% cash discount, and charges an additional 5% sales tax on the discounted price. If he sells 100 kg of goods (actual stock consumed), what is his total monetary profit?

A trader marks up his goods by 50%. He gives a 20% discount on cash sales. Moreover, due to spoliation, 10% of the goods become totally worthless and are discarded. What is his net percentage profit or loss?

A wholesale merchant buys an item at Rs. 100 per unit. He incurs 5% handling charges. He marks it up by 60% on total effective cost, offers a cash discount of 10%, charges 8% local tax on the discounted price, and uses a faulty measure delivering 5% less quantity. What is the net profit per unit sold?
A dealer sells an article at a profit of 20%. If he had bought it at 10% less and sold it for Rs. 12 less, he would have gained 25%. Find the cost price of the article.
